headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0071 — SMTO was asked for a Microsoft 365 permission it doesn't know

html:
SMTO-SKL-0071 — SMTO was asked for a Microsoft 365 permission it doesn't know

GUID: 7b1b5f4d-0577-556e-863a-aa0c5969b45e
Slug: microsoft365-feature-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • While connecting your Microsoft 365 account, SMTO was asked for a kind of access it doesn't support, so it didn't open the Microsoft sign-in. Nothing was connected or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Decide what SMTO needs: reading mail, writing mail, sending mail, calendar, contacts, OneDrive files, or SharePoint files, and whether it only reads or also makes changes. SMTO can only ask Microsoft for these specific kinds of access.
  2. Ask SMTO in a conversation to connect your Microsoft 365 account for just those, for example “connect my Microsoft account to read my calendar”. A clear request lets SMTO pick valid access names instead of an unsupported one.
  3. When SMTO shows the sign-in link, open it and approve Microsoft's consent page. The connection finishes only after you approve it on Microsoft's own page.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a Microsoft sign-in link, and after you approve it, SMTO says your account is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask for every kind of access just to avoid the error; request only what you need.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 consent preparation rejected the requested features: the value was not a list, or it contained a name outside the supported FEATURES table (mail_read, mail_write, mail_send, calendar_read, calendar_write, contacts_read, contacts_write, files_read, files_write, sharepoint_read, sharepoint_write).

What this means

  • Requested OAuth features are not a list/tuple or contain a feature outside the supported FEATURES registry. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Requested OAuth features are not a list/tuple or contain a feature outside the supported FEATURES registry.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested feature list with the advertised feature names.

How to fix it

  • The microsoft365.connect tool schema already limits features to supported names, so this usually comes from a direct POST /api/agent/microsoft365/auth/start call. Send features as a list containing only: mail_read, mail_write, mail_send, calendar_read, calendar_write, contacts_read, contacts_write, files_read, files_write, sharepoint_read, sharepoint_write, and only those the task needs (see src/agent_runtime/auth/microsoft/scopes.py FEATURES).
  • Replace invalid feature names with the required supported features before starting consent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Consent requests only the explicit supported features needed for the task.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
